background_notes.fact: For a vector u≠0 in a vector space over a field k, a·u=0 implies a=0. For a finite index type I, a family b:I→U is linearly independent precisely when every relation ∑_{i∈I} a_i·b_i=0 has all a_i=0.

background_notes.justification: If a≠0, multiplication of a·u=0 by a^{-1} gives u=0, a contradiction. Linear independence means that the kernel of the map taking a finitely supported coefficient family to its linear combination is zero. On finite I every coefficient family is finitely supported and this map is the displayed finite sum. Thus the coefficient extraction in S005 proves the required independence.
